name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3353: ci_sim exists to answer one question - does this test lean on something only his Mac has - and it was answering that question about names it had never loaded. MEASURED: asked for a class living in test_an_examined_panel_is_not_an_unread_one.py it raised AttributeError module test_control has no attribute, unittest wrapped that loader error as a _FailedTest, the runner counted it among errors, and the tail printed 1 test(s) depend on something only HIS machine has. THE TEST NEVER RAN. A name the tool cannot find is UNKNOWN, and turning it into a confident claim about his machine is the exact collapse the file was written to prevent, committed by the file itself. SECOND HALF, THE OVER-CLAIM: main() did import test_control and loaded names from that module ALONE while the banner read CI SIMULATION - the suite as a runner sees it, so every other test file was outside its reach and always had been. Both halves are fixed. Loader failures are now detected BEFORE anything counts them, and the tool exits 2 saying it could not LOAD the name and that this is UNKNOWN rather than a host dependency. The search falls through from test_control to whichever test file DEFINES the name. Every run prints its REACH, so no-known-host-dependency can be read against a population instead of floating free. Import failures during that search are swallowed deliberately: a module that cannot import here is not the subject of the question, and letting one bad file abort the scan would turn a findable class into an unfindable one. AND IT CORRECTED A STANDING CLAIM OF MINE, which is the more useful half: I had recorded that the four seal ERRORs on the CI-reds item are CI-ONLY, a VENUE fact, because they pass on his Mac. With the loader fixed that class runs 6 tests here and reports NO known host dependency - so passing locally plus tripping no known stub does not make something venue, it makes the cause UNMEASURED, which is a different word and the honest one. 476 gates, 5 cases, 3 red-proofs PROVEN.
